text:
Nobody drafted T.J. Hughes. He went from 57 points in 40 games at Michigan last season to a regular spot in Colorado's lineup, 20 games and counting at about 15 minutes a night, and the Colorado Springs Gazette is already writing about how he can stick long-term.

The goals have not come, and that is mostly bad luck. He has 2 goals on 5.8 expected and none in his last eleven games, despite 3.8 expected goals in that stretch. A 4.4% shooting rate is far below our range for him, and goals tend to follow chances. He has kept contributing anyway, with 6 assists in his last ten games, and 3 of his 9 points have come on the power play.

The part of his game to watch is at five on five, where Colorado is getting 47% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on, 6.3 points worse than without him. For an undrafted rookie, that is the number that decides whether he stays in the lineup. The goals are the part we would worry about least.
